title: Favorite trumpeters: Rene, Morgan and Chris Kelly on the corner
summary: He compares Kid Rene, Sam Morgan and Chris Kelly, and describes bands meeting on the corner and Rene handling rivals.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Just another minute or two on here, some of the bands that you played with you mentioned all these great trumpet players like Buddy Petit and Chris Kelly and Kid Rene, who was your favorite trumpet player in those days? Or Cornette, whatever they played.

Well uh, what was Cornette, that time Bill, Rene was the most jazzed man we had. I mean for fingering his corner and making those notes. And Sam Morgan was one of the sweetest trumpet players we had. But Chris Kelly, he had the ragged, ragged music you know, all the ragged music that people liked. The low class of people you know. Well he was king of that. I see many times we'd meet on the corner. Buddy Petit, Kid Rene, and Chris Kelly. We'd meet also Punch. Butch Miller, he was here, could tell you the same thing. They'd meet on the corner, George Boyd playing clarinet then. They'd meet on the corner. George Boyd playing clarinet there. And they'd meet on the corner. And stuff like

And they get there, at that time they didn't have trouble, they had news and where. They get together, they stay there. Stay there and play, watch Chiron Manila. Rene used to give a sign to go ahead, because Rene and Chris Keller's good friends, you see, he'd give Chris Keller a sign to go ahead and leave him to it. Chris would pull off, you see. And just leave Rene to handle that fella, because Rene could handle him. There was too much for Chris. We had a wonderful time, Bill. Show us some time whenever I was here now.

We didn't make much money, but we would be made, we'd done more with the money we made than we do with the money we make now. And then we had more work. The people I know, they respect us more, treat us more better.
Yeah, the musicians were popular then, I guess. Oh, Bill, you're talking about popular, Bill.
